title: Pseudo-coherence on a ringed site
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,J,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site small relative to the universe of module sheaves [def-weil-size-convention], with $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings and module category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $K\in D(\mathcal O)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and $m\in\mathbf Z$. Say $K$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent if for every $U\in\mathcal C$ there is a covering sieve $S$ on $U$ such that for every $f:V\to U$ in $S$ there is a bounded complex $P$ of $\mathcal O_V$-modules with degreewise finite-free splittings [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package] and a morphism $\alpha:Q(P)\to K|_V$ in $D(\mathcal O_V)$, using the canonical derived restriction [def-weil-pbc-ringed-site-derived-restriction], such that $H^j(\alpha)$ is an isomorphism for all $j>m$ and $H^m(\alpha)$ is an epimorphism. Say $K$ is pseudo-coherent if it is $m$-pseudo-coherent for every integer $m$. The covers and approximations may depend on $m$ and on the site object; bounds and ranks may vary with each covering member.
